calls.head: The Stars hunt better looks than the Predators
calls.body: On shot quality, Dallas is one of the league’s best and Nashville is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Stars’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Predators’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot was, Dallas had 4.3% a shot and Nashville 4.7% a shot. Coming in, Dallas was at 6.8% a shot and Nashville at 5.9% a shot.
calls.usual: DAL 6.8% a shot · NSH 5.9% a shot
calls.tonight: DAL 4.3% a shot · NSH 4.7% a shot

calls.head: The Stars’ power play outclasses the Predators’
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best and Nashville is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates more per 60 than the Predators’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On power-play expected goals per 60, Dallas had 13.9 per 60 and Nashville 3.8 per 60. Coming in, Dallas was at 8.6 per 60 and Nashville at 7.3 per 60.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (50% for Nashville), and Nashville came through.

DAL.head: We had this close to even (50% for Dallas), and it went Nashville’s way.

surprises.head: Dallas couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Dallas’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.8% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 80 games.
surprises.flipped: The Stars hunt better looks than the Predators

story.head: The Predators beat the Stars
paras: Miro Heiskanen opened the scoring 47 seconds in. Nils Hoglander scored the winner late in the first.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: One of the preview’s two calls held.
